content: Nicotine lozenges are prescribed to assist individuals in quitting smoking. These lozenges belong to a category of medications known as smoking cessation aids. They function by delivering nicotine to the body, which helps alleviate withdrawal symptoms that occur when smoking is stopped and reduces the craving to smoke. Nicotine lozenges are designed to dissolve slowly in the mouth. They should be used as directed on the packaging, typically at least 15 minutes after eating or drinking. It is important to follow the instructions carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the lozenges exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or fewer lozenges or use them more frequently than directed by your doctor. If you smoke your first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking up, you should use the 4 mg nicotine lozenges. If you smoke your first cigarette more than 30 minutes after waking, you should use the 2 mg lozenges. During weeks 1 to 6 of treatment, use one lozenge every 1 to 2 hours, ensuring you use at least nine lozenges per day to increase your chances of quitting. For weeks 7 to 9, use one lozenge every 2 to 4 hours. For weeks 10 to 12, use one lozenge every 4 to 8 hours. Do not use more than five lozenges in six hours or more than 20 lozenges per day. Avoid using more than one lozenge at a time or using them consecutively, as this can lead to side effects such as hiccups, heartburn, and nausea. To use the lozenge, place it in your mouth and allow it to dissolve slowly. Do not chew or swallow the lozenge. Occasionally, use your tongue to move the lozenge from one side of your mouth to the other. It should take 20 to 30 minutes to dissolve completely. Do not eat while the lozenge is in your mouth. Discontinue use after 12 weeks. If you still feel the need to use nicotine lozenges, consult your doctor. This medication may also be used for other conditions. Speak with your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using nicotine lozenges, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to nicotine or any other medications. Do not use nicotine lozenges if you are using other nicotine-based smoking cessation aids, such as patches, gum, inhalers, or nasal sprays. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention any non-nicotine smoking cessation aids, such as bupropion (Wellbutrin) or varenicline (Chantix), as well as medications for depression or asthma. Your doctor may need to adjust the dosages of your medications after you stop smoking. Inform your doctor if you have recently had a heart attack or if you have a history of heart disease, irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU), a genetic condition requiring a special diet to prevent intellectual disability. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using nicotine lozenges, contact your doctor immediately. It is essential to stop smoking completely while using nicotine lozenges. Continuing to smoke while using this medication may result in side effects. Seek advice and written information from your doctor or pharmacist to help you quit smoking. You are more likely to succeed in quitting if you receive information and support from your healthcare provider. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while using nicotine lozenges. Nicotine lozenges may cause mild side effects, such as heartburn or a sore throat. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as mouth problems or an irregular or fast heartbeat, require immediate medical attention. If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Store nicotine lozenges in their original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children and pets. Keep them at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store them in the bathroom). If you need to dispose of a lozenge, wrap it in paper and throw it away. Discard any medication that is outdated or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, diarrhea, weakness, and a fast heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor. If you have any questions about nicotine lozenges, consult your pharmacist.
